decision: Does transplanting LIFE's epsilon-Gram implicit correction (3-point delta + Gram system A*eps=1 + eps*ds*delta spreading) into TensorLBM's IBM force transfer reproduce the reference force-transfer fidelity, and what does the correction buy vs the uncorrected in-repo baseline?

alternatives.A1_life_transplant: TensorLBM IBM force spread WITH LIFE epsilon-Gram correction: LIFE 3-point delta, A*eps=1 solved per body, spread weight = eps*ds*diracVal (OSS semantics, line-cited)
alternatives.A2_uncorrected_control: Same LIFE 3-point delta, epsilon=1 (no correction) -- isolates the correction as the single changed variable
alternatives.A3_inrepo_baseline: TensorLBM existing ibm_force_spread (hat / 4pt kernel, no correction) -- the current in-repo baseline for the difference list

hypothesis: H1: the epsilon-Gram correction drives the force-transfer round-trip (spread then interpolate) error to ~machine precision and conserves total deposited force, whereas the uncorrected arm (A2) shows a kernel-normalisation error O(delta discretisation). H0 (falsifier): A1 round-trip error >= 1e-6 OR A1 total-force conservation error >= 15%.

metrics.total_force_conservation_rel: |sum_j F_grid_j - sum_m f_m ds_m| / |sum_m f_m ds_m| (x and y separately)
metrics.epsilon_stats: min/max/mean of epsilon across markers (diagnostic: how far from 1 the correction is)

unit_of_analysis: one (marker_layout, force_field, arm) configuration; KPIs are scalars

baseline_control.physical_baseline: the target marker force field itself (exact, zero hand-copy): round-trip reference is the input force
baseline_control.representation_control: A1 vs A2 share the identical LIFE 3-point delta kernel, identical marker layout, identical ds; the ONLY changed variable is epsilon (solved vs 1)
baseline_control.oss_note: LIFE is a C++ LBM-IBM-FEM FSI solver requiring LAPACK/Boost and a full FSI case; this environment runs the semantics-exact transplant of its delta kernel, support build, Gram system and spreading rule (cited line by line) into TensorLBM, not an execution of the OSS binary. Recorded as a comparison limit, not silently upgraded.

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: H1 holds iff A1 round-trip L2 rel < 1e-6 AND A1 total-force conservation rel < 1e-6; the 15% owner band is the acceptance floor for any physics KPI, but the correction is a representation/normalisation fix so it is held to a 1e-6 identity threshold (6 orders stricter) because a normalisation fix must be exact
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: a KPI is spacing-converged when |KPI(N=32)-KPI(N=16)|/|KPI(N=32)| < 5%; otherwise the finer value is reported and the spacing delta is reported as a sensitivity result

stopping_rule: round-trip arms are single-shot (no time integration); the physics arm (cylinder drag) runs a fixed predeclared step count and stops early only on the predeclared steady criterion; no arm is extended after looking at KPIs. Wall-clock budget 900 s per arm on CPU; anything above moves to the cluster queue.
variables_changed: epsilon (solved Gram system vs 1) -- the correction under test
force field (constant (1,0) vs radial (cos,sin)) -- field sensitivity
variables_held_fixed: LIFE 3-point delta kernel (identical in A1 and A2)
marker layout (circle of radius R=10 in a 64x64 periodic grid, center (32,32))

physics_arm.case: 2D fixed cylinder in uniform flow, force-based IBM, Re=100 (u=0.1, D=8, nu=0.08 -> tau=0.53)
physics_arm.reference: time-averaged drag coefficient Cd vs literature band for 2D cylinder at Re=100 (Cd ~ 1.5-2.0)
physics_arm.arms: A1 (epsilon-Gram corrected force spread) vs A2 (uncorrected)
physics_arm.note: secondary physics arm; the round-trip/conservation arm is the primary XVAL of the correction

analysis: report A1 vs A2 vs A3 per KPI with explicit pass/fail vs the predeclared thresholds; distinguish the correction effect (A1 vs A2) from the kernel effect (A2 vs A3); no threshold tuning after seeing results
safety_resource_limits: CPU float64, single process, 900 s wall-clock budget per arm; cluster queue for anything heavier
